content: This medication may cause dizziness or drowsiness. Consuming alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can intensify these effects. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or engaging in activities that require alertness until you are certain you can perform them safely. Refrain from consuming alcoholic beverages, and be aware that some liquid medications may contain alcohol. Exercise caution if you have diabetes, alcohol dependence, liver disease, or any condition requiring limited alcohol intake. For individuals with diabetes, this medication may make it more challenging to manage blood sugar levels. Regularly monitor your blood sugar as directed and share the results with your doctor. Notify your doctor immediately if you experience high or low blood sugar levels. Children may be more susceptible to side effects such as muscle spasms or uncontrolled muscle movements. Older adults may also be more sensitive to this medication, particularly experiencing drowsiness, tardive dyskinesia (a movement disorder), or Parkinson’s-like muscle problems. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when absolutely necessary. It passes into breast milk and may have undesirable effects on a nursing infant. Drug interactions can alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not list all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Metoclopramide accelerates the movement of food and medication through your stomach, which may affect the absorption of certain drugs. Check the labels of all your medications, such as allergy or cough-and-cold products, as they may contain ingredients that cause drowsiness. In the event of an overdose with serious symptoms like passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. While taking this medication, your doctor may recommend lab or medical tests, such as an endoscopy for ulcers. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This medication is used to treat certain stomach and intestinal conditions. It is prescribed as a short-term treatment (4 to 12 weeks) for persistent heartburn when other medications are not effective. It is primarily used for heartburn that occurs after meals or during the daytime. Metoclopramide is also used in diabetic patients with delayed stomach emptying (gastroparesis), which can help reduce symptoms such as nausea, vomiting, and abdominal fullness. It works by blocking a natural substance in the body (dopamine). This medication is not recommended for use in children due to an increased risk of serious side effects, such as muscle spasms or uncontrolled movements. Read the medication guide provided by your pharmacist before starting metoclopramide and each time you get a refill. Take this medication by mouth as directed by your doctor, usually up to four times daily (30 minutes before meals and at bedtime). The dosage is based on your medical condition, response to treatment, age, and other medications you may be taking. If heartburn occurs only at specific times (e.g., after the evening meal), your doctor may advise taking a single dose before those times instead of throughout the day. For diabetic gastroparesis, this medication is typically taken for 2 to 8 weeks until your stomach functions properly. This condition may recur periodically, and your doctor may instruct you to restart the medication when symptoms reappear and stop when you feel better. Take this medication regularly as directed to gain the most benefit. If you suddenly stop using this medication, you may experience withdrawal symptoms such as dizziness, nervousness, or headaches. To prevent withdrawal, your doctor may gradually reduce your dose. Withdrawal is more likely if you have used metoclopramide for a long time or in high doses. Common side effects include drowsiness, dizziness, fatigue, trouble sleeping, agitation, headache, and diarrhea. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare. If you experience any unusual or severe symptoms, contact your doctor immediately. Before taking metoclopramide, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that can cause allergic reactions or other problems. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
